builder_plan.scenario: A narrow, repeated product task may not need your largest model.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a released student model fits the task before generating training data.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model and an off-the-shelf small model on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Student quality, serving cost, teacher calls, training cost, and failures on unusual inputs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Replay, Don't Resample: Off-Policy Consolidation of Long-Horizon RL Experts
summary: MRPD replaces multi-teacher on-policy distillation for consolidating per-domain RL experts by replaying the experts' logged rollouts, sampling probabilities, and rewards through the student, recomputing policy gradients and distilling final-expert distributions at logged prefixes. It requires no environment, reward model, or sampling during consolidation, so the only costs are trainer compute (roughly one seventh of expert training) and the storage and retention of complete, ordered expert logs. It can fail if logs lack sampling probabilities or ordering metadata, if the student architecture diverges enough from the experts that quasi-on-policy assumptions break, or if expert drift and domain shift make the final experts' distributions poor distillation targets.
rationale: The method only pays off if the team already runs multi-domain RL post-training and retains complete expert logs, which is plausible but not guaranteed at this infrastructure scale, so it warrants a small-scale pilot rather than direct adoption.

claims.statement: MRPD replaces multi-teacher on-policy distillation for consolidating per-domain RL experts by replaying the experts' logged rollouts, sampling probabilities, and rewards through the student, recomputing policy gradients and distilling final-expert distributions at logged prefixes. It requires no environment, reward model, or sampling during consolidation, so the only costs are trainer compute (roughly one seventh of expert training) and the storage and retention of complete, ordered expert logs. It can fail if logs lack sampling probabilities or ordering metadata, if the student architecture diverges enough from the experts that quasi-on-policy assumptions break, or if expert drift and domain shift make the final experts' distributions poor distillation targets.

Consolidating experts costs about one seventh of the compute used to train them, and the student surpasses multi-teacher on-policy distillation from the same experts at a fraction of MOPD's cost on three long-horizon agentic domains (reasoning, search, SQL).
